I initially ordered their long handled tea infusers and while they worked, they weren't exactly what i needed. I make hot tea with fresh mint leaves, fresh grated ginger, fennel seeds, etc. I wanted something that kept my ingredients out of my drinking tea but infused them with the flavor. I also wanted something that was easy to clean. These fit the bill perfectly! The company actually reached out to me and recommend I try these since I didn't completely love their other product. How awesome is that? It's nice to know that The Friendly Swede cares about their customers and want you to be happy with their products and provide personalized recommendations.

These mesh tea infusers are easy to use and seal up well with the ingredients. They have a small clasp on the side that slides in and closes the two halves together. This also makes it easy to clean since the entire thing opens up when you are done and I never have to worry about grated ginger or small fennel seeds getting stuck in there. These also have a hook at the end so you can place it on the tip of your cup so when you are ready to remove the infuser, you don't have to dig it out. Simply unhook it from your cup and remove it.

I am so happy with these and have been using them daily since I received them. That in addition to the follow-up from the company have made me a happy customer. I wouldn't hesitate to buy these again or other products from them.

Unless this product is JUST used for the purpose of your dryer turning on when you close the dryer door, then YES, this product did fix our dryer in terms of it turning on when the dryer door was shut.  HOWEVER..... if you open the dryer door during the drying cycle... it will NOT turn the dryer off.  It will KEEP going, it will continue to rotate the dryer drum while the door is wide open!  Your dryer will NOT turn off unless you physically turn the drying cycle off with the cycle selection knob.  I feel that this product is NOT safe to be used in homes where the dryer will be in use around small children.

My story (no need to read but maybe it will help someone else)

I have a Kenmore 400 series, model # 110.67442600 dryer. For me the light bulb stopped working a couple of years ago (no big deal), then about a year ago I noticed that the dryer wouldn't stop while mid-cycle if you popped the door open, again no big deal. And this week the dryer wouldn't turn on even though there was power to it.

After researching dryer troubleshooting websites and youtube I checked first the breaker and the outlet, then the dryer itself (door switch, push to start button, thermal fuse). I knew it was probably the door switch and after testing it, it was.

I purchased this switch to replace the dryer door switch on my old Whirlpool dryer (model number LEQ9030PQ0). I recognized that when I would shut the door and attempt to start the dryer it would not start. After many various attempts (such as slamming the door, slowly closing the door, etc.), I finally recognized that if I lifted on the handle as I closed the door that it would finally shut. Then I noticed on the top right of the inside of the dryer that there was a little black latch. And that the latch was actually broken. If I pressed on it, I would hear a click. I pressed the latch and then attempted to start the dryer and it would start! Because the latch was broken off, it wasn't long enough for the door to close on it, causing the dryer to not recognize that the door was closed. That's where this part comes into play...

This switch was quickly shipped, packaged well and functioned perfectly. Very easy to install (given where the part is). Switch was made of a heavy duty plastic, which appears to be a better quality than the original that came on my dryer.

Pros:
-Least expensive unit available with Prime shipping
-1/3 the price of OEM replacement from manufacturer
-Exact fit for cutout and mounting holes in dryer
Cons:
-Dryer door needed spacer to activate switch (but easy to fix)
-Studs holding switch together just melted with soldering iron leading to questions regarding quality. See photo.
-Wires slightly shorter than on OEM unit. (but not really a problem) See photo.
Details.
Purchased for Maytag Dryer MEDX500XW0 (switch used on many makes and models). I accidentally broke the original switch while replacing the dryer's rollers and drive belt. The OEM switch is only glued together and a hard yank on the wires pulled it apart. Prime is addictive. I was willing to wait two days to save ten dollars when compared with local price.
The OEM unit has three studs in one half with matching holes in the other. In the OEM unit the studs are only used to keep the two halves in alignment. The switch is held together with urethane glue. On the purchased unit no glue is used. Instead, the three stud ends are melted with a soldering iron to hold the two halves together. (see photo). It might not make any difference but one starts to question where and how this switch is put together.
